//: period is in ns; 14.286ns == 70MHz, matching info.yaml's clock_hz. 70 MHz is where 10 Mbit Ethernet gets 7 clocks a bit (the measured tolerance in design_rationale Deviation 11); the 50 MHz harden closed with setup WNS +7.3 ns, and its critical path (SRAM read at the slow corner, ~12.4 ns) left ~1.6 ns of predicted slack at 70 MHz before resizing. Fallbacks if any corner fails setup or hold: 60 MHz (16.667), then 50 MHz (20).
//tmpl0: -- Baseline tunables adopted from TinyTapeout/ttihp-verilog-template@cmos5l's src/config.json (the project's own maintained default for this PDK), not re-derived from the old sg13g2 config -- this PDK may need different defaults than sg13g2 did and there's no reason to guess when the vendor's own template states them directly.
//pnr: PNR_CORNERS: LibreLane's default (null) runs the place-and-route resizer against DEFAULT_CORNER only, the typical corner. The 70 MHz attempt showed the cost: post-CTS repair drove typical to exactly 0 ns while the slow corner, never optimized, finished at -13 ns. Listing all three STA corners makes setup repair see the slow corner and hold repair the fast one.
//hold: GRT hold margin raised from the template's 0.05 to 0.1: the 50 MHz harden finished with hold WNS +0.057 ns at the fast corner (flop -> SRAM A_ADDR, and the macro's fast lib is characterized at -55C, not the -40C corner), so a re-placement could tip it negative.
//0c: DPL_CELL_PADDING=1 (site-widths, one site = 480nm here) adds a small gap between every pair of adjacent standard cells during detailed placement. On the old sg13g2 target this closed the last 15 Magic DRC violations (long-parallel-run M2/M3 spacing near the SRAM macro's BIST/test-pin tie-off cells). Kept as a sensible default for CMOS5L too -- free at this design's low die utilization, not yet re-verified whether CMOS5L reproduces the same residual.
//0d: Electrical-rule cleanup (signoff STA warnings; timing was already met). (a) Fanout: the CMOS5L stdcell libs declare default_max_fanout 8, but LibreLane's MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT defaults to 10, so the resizer left 3 nets at fanout 10, and CTS's default sink clusters left 28 leaf clock buffers at fanout 11-19. Both now target 8. (b) Slew/cap on the SRAM macro pins: repair_design only ran after global placement, on estimated wires. Routed parasitics at the slow corner then pushed 14 SRAM input pins (mostly uE1's address/WEN nets, each shared by two macros) over max-slew, and 2-3 A_DOUT outputs over the macro's 0.064 pF max-cap. The macros sit in one row along the die bottom, so these nets are long: uE1's write-enable was 913 um on a single buf_1, and most SRAM address/data nets 550-900 um. Hold fixing also puts weak dlygate4sd3_1 delay cells in front of the address pins, each then driving ~290-320 um. Fix, in order of what each step bought: RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR + 30% placement margins cleared cap and fanout but left 18 slew; MAX_WIRE_LENGTH 300 (default 0 = off, lets the resizer split long wires) fixed the 913 um net; post-GRT margin 50% (global-route estimates under-call the routed slew of these nets by ~1.5-2x) cleared uE1, leaving 12 on uE0; MAX_WIRE_LENGTH 200 cleared the rest. Result: 0 slew/cap/fanout at all three corners, setup WNS +7.34 ns, hold WNS +0.057 ns, 4,018 cells (+314), 2.01 mW (+0.26).
//0: FP_SIZING must be 'absolute' for a fixed-die-size project like Tiny Tapeout -- LibreLane's default 'relative' ignores the explicit DIE_AREA from tt_tool.py --create-user-config and computes its own die size from FP_CORE_UTIL/FP_ASPECT_RATIO instead. Root-caused against sg13g2 (the 'design area shrinks partway through the flow' finding); the cmos5l template's own config.json sets this too, for the same reason.
//1: -- Real IHP SRAM macro integration (RM_IHPSG13_1P_512x8_c3_bm_bist), same part as sg13g2 -- ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.ref/sg13cmos5l_sram is a symlink to sg13g2_sram in the CMOS5L PDK install (confirmed identical LEF SIZE 236.8 x 110.38um). Four instances: mue0/mue1 (uE0 phys / uE1 protocol engines) x lo/hi (low/high byte of the 16-bit instruction word). Paths repointed at the CMOS5L PDK install (~/ttsetup/pdk_cmos5l), not the old sg13g2-only one (~/ttsetup/pdk) -- see docs/design/design_rationale.txt's CRITICAL FINDING section.
//1a: lib corner temps are the macro's own vendor characterization points, not an exact match to this design's STA_CORNERS -- wildcarded by speed class (typ/fast/slow), unchanged reasoning from the sg13g2 config.
//1b: instance placement: each macro is 236.8 x 110.38um. All four sit in ONE row along the core bottom, orientation FS (flipped). Why: in the macro's own (N) frame, every signal pin is on the bottom edge (Metal2), while the top edge carries all three PG nets (VSS!, the 4 full-height VDD!, all VDDARRAY!) and no signals. FS turns that power edge to face down into a ~10um channel above the core bottom (y=3.78..14) where src/pdn_macro_bridge.tcl draws the Metal3 straps + Metal4 stubs, and turns the signal edge to face up into the open logic area. (The old 2x2 N stack pointed mue*_lo's signal edge at the die boundary with ~6um to spare -- the likely cause of v5's bottom-band routing congestion.) y=14 keeps the channel entirely inside FP_MACRO_VERTICAL_HALO (10um) so no standard-cell rows survive underneath the macros.
//1b2: x = 10 / 280 / 580 / 880: each ~33um gap is wide enough (after PDN_VERTICAL_HALO=10 on both sides) to keep one full-height VPWR+VGND stripe pair (x=262.88/266.98, 562.88/566.98, 862.88/866.98), so every macro has stripes a short strap run away on both sides. The old 50um-pitch phase-alignment rule no longer applies -- macro pins no longer need to line up with stripes, the bridge straps do the connecting.
//1c: EXTRA_VERILOG_MODELS points at a hand-trimmed blackbox stub (dir::RM_IHPSG13_1P_512x8_c3_bm_bist_blackbox.v), NOT the vendor's own behavioral .v -- that file's specify block uses SDF timing-check syntax Yosys's Verilog-2005 frontend can't parse, and it's irrelevant for synthesis anyway (only the port list matters; LEF/GDS/LIB carry the physical/timing views). Same file as the sg13g2 config -- the macro's port list is identical, so no changes needed here.
//1d: PDN_CFG points at a patched copy of librelane 3.1.0.dev3's default pdn_cfg.tcl (extracted from the librelane/librelane:3.1.0.dev3 container itself): the macro-grid block is removed (it can only ever produce PDN-0232 here -- the macro pins are on Metal4, which is also the tile's top routing layer and its only PDN layer), and it sources src/pdn_macro_bridge.tcl, which wraps pdngen and draws the macro power connections itself. See both files for the reasoning.
//2: -- PDN hookup: connects each macro instance's own power pins (VDD!/VSS!/VDDARRAY! -- see the macro's LEF) to this design's top-level PDN grid nets (VPWR/VGND, per this PDK's libs.tech/librelane/config.tcl VDD_PIN/GND_PIN). VDDARRAY! is tied to the same VPWR rail -- single-supply design, not a separate voltage domain. Unchanged from the sg13g2 config -- the macro's pin names don't depend on which PDK install it's loaded from.
//3: -- Magic DRC blackbox for the SRAM macro (MAGIC_DRC_MAGLEFS). Still required on CMOS5L: Magic DRC against the real macro GDS gives 120,951 SRAM-interior errors (CMOS5L's SRAMID exemptions don't cover Magic's whole deck). The file is generated under the CMOS5L tech by scripts/maglef/gen_maglef.tcl (Magic 'lef read' of the vendor LEF), then post-processed by scripts/maglef/trim_maglef.py, which clips the solid obsm2/obsm3 blocks back 1.5um from the signal-pin edge and lengthens the Metal2 pin stubs to min area -- without that, Magic flags every wire landing on a macro pin (M2.f/M3.f wide-metal spacing, M2.d) although the real GDS is clean. Only Magic DRC reads this file; the router uses the vendor LEF, and TT precheck for CMOS5L runs the KLayout ihp-sg13cmos5l.drc deck on the real GDS (clean), not Magic.
//4: PDN_OBSTRUCTIONS: TT precheck's pin check needs every VPWR/VGND LEF port rectangle to reach within 10um of BOTH the bottom and top die edge. pdngen cuts each Metal4 stripe around the SRAM row (y=14..124.38), leaving segments that start at y~124.9 -- 40 of them failed 'too far from bottom edge'. Blocking Metal4 stripes over each macro column above the macro (x = macro x0 .. x0+236.8, y = 124.4 .. die top 710.64) means only the full-height stripes in the gaps beside the macros survive; the standard-cell rails above the macros are fed from those. Applies only during PDN generation (removed again before routing).
